description: Tournons La Page search results identify a scanned Niamey municipal order no. 0006/PDS/VN/SG dated 25 January prohibiting an MNPD march followed by a meeting planned for Wednesday 27 January, for public-order risk. The linked 18.77 MB report PDF could not be read, and the only detailed indexed copy is a third-party mirror of the same report. It remains unknown whether people assembled despite the ban, what demand they planned to press, and whether 50 or more attended.
required_followup: Search contemporary Nigerien media and public notices for 26–28 January for evidence of an actual assembly or cancellation; if no report is found, retain this as an unconfirmed banned plan and do not infer attendance.

description: A search-only Bénin Web TV result describes an opposition-coalition meeting at Niamey’s Palais des sports on 12 January with more than 3,000 attendees. It frames the meeting as an electoral coalition appeal against the governing-party candidate. The full source remains unavailable after Cache miss and a DNS failure on ordinary HTTPS retry; the exact event day, whether it was a public protest rather than an electoral support meeting, and whether it demanded state action remain unverified. An opened 11 January ANP article documents only an opposition declaration and a call for future mobilization, not an assembly.
required_followup: Find a contemporary Niger source for the 12 January meeting; establish whether it was a public protest demanding state action or an electoral support rally/meeting before coding or excluding it.

description: Le Sahel/ONEP reports a RJRN anniversary and youth-exchange gathering in Niamey on 24 January. The article records a request that government increase job creation and training, but reports no venue, public access, attendance or protest format. Its celebratory and election-conflict-prevention context leaves open whether this was a protest action.
required_followup: Search contemporary RJRN/Le Sahel/ANP and other local coverage or public notices for the meeting venue, participant count, event format, and whether the government request was pressed as a public protest.
